the development and application of structured Bayesian models that can exploit the underlying structure of the observed and/or latent data to improve computational tractability and predictive accuracy.
the design and analysis of efficient algorithms for Bayesian inference in Gaussian processes latent variable models (GP-LVMs).

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we introduce a Bayesian Gaussian Process Latent Variable model with structured spatial covariance and show how to perform scalable inference and prediction on this model.
we introduce a Bayesian GP-LVM with spatial correlations that can be used to impute missing data on high-dimensional systems.
we have developed a new Bayesian Gaussian process latent variables model that can be used in a number of different ways.

the model can be made tractable for large-scale problems through a structured variational bound.
structure-exploiting methods for Gaussian process latent variable modeling are not limited to the case of a single Gaussian likelihood.
